Bro. Penny submitted the report of the majority of the Committee
appointed by the last Convention to consider the advisability of a new Fra
ternity Song Book, which was referred to the Committee on Unfinished Bus
iness. The report is as follows:�
In looking over the ground carefully, and getting the opinion of many of
the chapters, we would earnestly recommend an entire new edition of the
Fraternity Song Book which would embody the following improvements:
We find that many of the songs were written by persons who had but
little knowledge of music beyond the mere
melody accompanying the words,
hence some are written in keys too high, others in keys too low for ordinary
voices. In many the harmony could be greatly improved. We therefore re
commend the rearrangement and transposition of many of the songs, the har
monizing of others of which the melody only is published, and their better
adaptation to male voices.
That many of the songs be arranged for Quartette or Chorus purpos
es, giving each voice a
seperated stave. This would aid greatly in the encourage
ment of chapter singing.
That anumber of new songs, which have been written sincethel.stedition of the book, be included in the new edition. Of these, about 26 are
now in existence and a number of others oould undoubtedly be obtained.
That all instrumental music be excluded.
Some beautiful songs are set to music entirely inappropriate to the
sentiment of the poems, and on that account are never sung. We would recom
mend the substitution of original music for some of the hackneyed Moody
and Sankey tunes.
We recommend that the size of the pages be increased, making a
larger sized book.
7th.�
Several of the chapters have songs local in character ; we would re
commend the introduction of a local chapter song department.
8lh�
A new grouping of the songs according to their character is deemed
advisable.
That music be put to some of the best songs where the air is indica
ted only by the name.
10th. �
That some songs, which are never
sung, should be omitted alto
gether, or at least be confined to the words only, with the air indicated ; also
that some songs found in the earlier editions, but omitted in the latter ones, be
included according to the judgment of the compilers.
11th. �
We would also recommend the publication of a pocket edition of the
Fraternity Songs without the music, in paper covers, which could be sold at a
low price.
These recommendations would do away with the old plates and would re-

B
quire an entire new set. As to the comparative cost of publication, the Com
mittee not having considted with publishing firms, are not at present prepar
ed to state.
Very EespectfuUy,
(Signed)
W. D. Holmes (X '81) )

THE ANNUAL COMMUNICATION OF THE EXECUTIVE COUNCIL TO
THE FIFTY-SECOND GENEEAL CONVENTION.
1. Membership List. �
Under Gen. Ees. No. 2, of 1884, the CouncU selected
Bro.Wm. M. Kingsley (A, '83), to supervisethe work of preparing and publish
ing, under the direction of the Council, a Ust of the members of the Fraternity.
In October, 1884, notices were sent to each Chapter requesting the appoint
ment of an editor, who wotUd secure and be responsible for the complete and
accurate list of his Chapter's membership, with such information as was called
for by the resolution. Instructions were given at the same time, under author
ity of the Council, that the lists should be forwarded to the Council on or
before January 15th, 1885. After considerable delay aU the Chapters ap
pointed editors, and the work was begun. At the date mentioned only three
lists had been received, and an extension of time was found necessary ; but
inasmuch as on the 1st of March several of the Chapter lists were still lacking,
it was found impossible to publish the list before the time of the Convention,
and it was accordingly decided to send none of the manuscript to the printer,
but to await the decision of another Convention. The matter therefore stands
as foUows :
�
The Chapter lists are in the hands of the CouncU. In general,
the lists are fairly complete, but in many instances no trace of members has
been found, and nothing later than the information in the catalogue of 1879 is
given. If the manuscript in its present condition were
printed, the result
would be a membership list which would be of service and value, but which
would by no means approach the accuracy of the last General Catalogue, or be
calculated to stand the criticisms and comparisons to which it would be sub
jected.
The catalogue of 1879 is out of print. Its accuracy and completeness down
to the time of its date, together with the continued demand for it, seem to jus
tify a new edition, which can readily be printed from the old plates. If, in
addition, a supplement be issued, similar in style, containing the names of
members not included in the original work, the whole vriU form a uniform and
complete membership roU, which the Council beUeves wiU be more satisfac
tory, and can be pubUshed more speedily and at less cost, than the entire
new Ust called for by the last Convention.
In any event, whatever be ihe form of the work determined upon, the Coun
cil ventures to suggest that in matters of detaU fuU discretion be given it, ex
perience having shown that a compUanee with some of the requirements of
Gen. Res. No. 2, ot 1884, would detract from the merits of the proposed list.
2. Fraternity Records. �
In connection with the work on the Member
ship List during the past year, the Council has undertaken to make for its own
archives a record of the membership of the Fraternity since the date of the
last catalogue, including symbols, offices, and such other information as
may
be furnished by the Chapters. Until a late period this Council has had no
official Ust or record of membership of any kind except the Chapter reports ren
dered since October, 1883. The usefulness and need of such a Ust is apparent.

13
The defect has been partly overcome
by the recent purchase of a copy of the
catalogue of 1879. In order thai; the record may be continued and maintained,
the co-operation of the Chapters must be had, and the CouncU requests that
the Chapters hereafter report changes in membership and offices immediately
upon their occurrence^ The reports due on November 1 of each year, under
the Constitution, serve only as the basis for levying the annual taxes ; in prac
tice, they are incomplete in many important particulars, and the delay and ir
regularity in forwarding them greatly impair their value. Of the reports
which were due on November 1, 1884, only two were received at the proper
time, viz : those from the Delta and Beta ; six were received during the
month of November, three in December, five in January, 1885, one in Febru
ary, and one in March.

with the Beta Chapter, relating to the conduct of Mr. Lewis Sherrill Bigelow

and has Tbecome a member of the Sigma Phi Fraternity. The Phi claims that
Mr Bigelow has violated the constitution. The constitution, however, does
not forbid such double membership ; but Mr. Bigelow must be regarded as a
member of the Phi Chapter, according to Article 6, Section 6, which provides
that
'�
Any brother leaving the Chapter into which he was initiated, and be
coming a member of any coUege in which there is or shaU be a Chapter of this
Fraternity, shaU be considered an active member of the last named Chapter,
and, as such, subject to its discipline." The Phi has complete jurisdiction,
therefore, and may dispose of the case according to its own rules.
